title: NR-V04 covalent input admissibility — does ANY co-fold seat celastrol within bonding distance of the preregistered site?
terminus: ✅ CLOSED with a REFUSAL, and the refusal is the result. Prereg AMENDMENT 1's criterion A1 requires a covalent leg to stage its electrophilic carbon within bonding distance of the TARGET-chain Cys Sγ. The amendment's own conclusion rested on `nrv04_prespend_check._pull_model`, which samples ONE model per system out of a seed ENSEMBLE; this lane re-measured A1 on EVERY model of EVERY system of every co-fold prefix, and separated 'passes at the NEAREST cysteine' from 'passes at the FROZEN site (NR4A1 C551)' — a distinction the prespend check cannot make. Result: `n_models_passing_A1: 0` of 3, C551 distances 34.42 / 29.87 / 39.11 Å against an 8.0 Å limit, and the verdict recorded verbatim is *"EVERY covalent-arm model FAILS the A1 tether gate — build_system RAISES, so these legs cannot run at all"*. ⛔ So the covalent arm is not unrun, it is UNRUNNABLE on every available input. The companion adduct-construction job exists precisely because the co-folds cannot supply an admissible input; a hand-built preformed Michael adduct at the literature site (Zhang 2018, doi:10.1039/C8CC06140H) would fix the COMPARISON without supplying the EVIDENCE. Both jobs are $0 CPU.
